questionText: The chip select logic for a certain DRAM chip in a memory system design is shown below. Assume that the memory system has 16 address lines denoted by $A_{15}$ to $A_{0}$. What is the range of addresses (in hexadecimal) of the memory system that can get enabled by the chip select (CS) signal?
explanation:
To enable the chip select ($CS$) signal, the output of the 5-input AND gate must be $1$.

From the circuit diagram:
• $A_{15}$ is directly connected $\implies A_{15} = 1$
• $A_{14}$ is directly connected $\implies A_{14} = 1$
• $A_{13}$ is connected via an inverter (bubble) $\implies A_{13} = 0$
• $A_{12}$ is connected via an inverter (bubble) $\implies A_{12} = 0$
• $A_{11}$ is directly connected $\implies A_{11} = 1$

Thus, the higher order bits are fixed as:
$A_{15} A_{14} A_{13} A_{12} A_{11} = 11001_2$

The remaining lower order address lines ($A_{10}$ to $A_0$) can vary from all $0$'s to all $1$'s.

Minimum Address:
Binary: $1100\ 1000\ 0000\ 0000_2$
Hexadecimal: $\text{C800}_{16}$

Maximum Address:
Binary: $1100\ 1111\ 1111\ 1111_2$
Hexadecimal: $\text{CFFF}_{16}$

Hence, the address range enabled by $CS$ is C800 to CFFF.
